terra.problem: Bronze from head to toe adds coverage the text does not specify, and Goliath's desire not to be hit is an unmarked guess.
The text does not say Goliath has no gold on him.
Saying Papa is the only one in the story standing on gold puts him in a Bible event.
The whole valley watching and everyone else sitting and holding their breath are invented scene details.
The closing comparison is unclear: Goliath is the giant, so who does not need a crowd to fight him?
The army staring at its feet and the absence of a speech or plan are not stated.
The joke makes the frightened Israelites the target of the laugh.
Nobody pulling out a map is an invented detail about the Israelites.
The back-of-things callback does not explain Papa's time in the drawer, so a baker unfamiliar with his story lacks its setup.
The passage says Goliath took his stand morning and evening, but does not say he gave the same speech twice every day.
The passage does not say Israel heard the same challenge twice a day for forty days.
The text does not say the line broke the moment Goliath appeared or that forty days of his voice would shake anybody.
Referring to the next card exposes the lesson's structure.
Saying the tax part is coming up exposes the lesson's structure.
The closing joke relies on a family stereotype about brothers.
The explanation makes the army's flight simultaneous with David's offer to Saul; the passage does not say that.
David isn't going anywhere contradicts his offer to go and fight Goliath.
The text says David was not accustomed to the gear, not that it did not fit or that he had never worn armor.
Saying Goliath is about to learn a lesson about judging by looks adds an outcome the text does not give.
The passage does not say Goliath was insulted by a sling; he speaks of David coming at him with sticks.
David says the whole world will know there is a God in Israel; he does not say the world is invited to see it.
The passage does not say Goliath trusted his weapons.
The text does not say the Philistines' whole plan was built around Goliath.
The passage gives the extent of the pursuit but does not say the Philistines ran toward their own cities.
David's emotional state is not given; saying he was just polite contrasts him with people who would be shaken.
The light comparison about being shaken is attached to David holding Goliath's severed head, making a violent detail part of the joke.
